observations.fact: Negative y indices read the trigger bank at0x27e88b8; positive y indices read the separate bank at0x257c9d8.
Each matching enabled ProcessERM handler saves the trigger bank. Events numbered>=30000 clear it before checking conditions; FU handlers keep the inherited values.
The saved trigger bank is restored after that handler. Positive FU/DO locals are a separate bank and must not be cleared at these boundaries.

implementation: Only negative y cells reset before each non-FU trigger condition. Positive y cells remain shared across matching handlers.
Each FU handler inherits the caller trigger cells anew; nested functions and DO iterations cannot leak their negative writes back into the caller or sibling handler.
Suspended commands retain both banks until the current handler completes. No continuation field or native save-format change.
validation: Sanitized native C++ executor: paused command resumption, fresh trigger conditions, shared positive cells, inherited negative cells, nested FU restoration and sibling FU handlers.

Private WebAssembly controls wrap unchanged original potion BA0/BA1 and FU800..816 blocks. Chromium and WebKit verify boundary0/55 and nested7/99/99/7/7/99/42 through a real nested battle and native dialogue barriers.
All12 original compiled campaign programs contain no negative y operands; their positive y sharing is preserved, including the seven matching FU100 handlers ofzc1-2.
limitations: The evidence concerns supported integer y cells; it does not establish floating-point ERM bank support.
Private controls and the final906 save are not a new original campaign completion or a mid-battle save admission.
